# LS Exit Audit v0.3.0 — Purchase Terms

Effective November 22, 2026.

## Price and payment

The price is **US$29 one time**, accepted as **29 USDT on the TRON network (TRC20)**. The buyer is responsible for network fees and for selecting the exact token and network. Payments sent using another asset, network, or address may be unrecoverable.

## License scope

A purchase grants one buyer or one organization a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use LS Exit Audit v0.3.0 internally on repositories and URLs the buyer owns or is authorized to inspect. Redistribution, resale, sublicensing, public mirroring, and sharing the package outside the purchasing organization are not included. For a paid, named buyer, these purchase terms and the private delivery confirmation govern the granted internal-use right if a bundled pre-release evaluation notice conflicts with them.

## Delivery

After the payment is confirmed on-chain, the buyer receives the v0.3.0 ZIP, its SHA-256 checksum, and quick-start instructions through the private delivery route agreed in the purchase request. No paid ZIP or source code is hosted in this public sales repository.

## Refunds

Because this is a digitally delivered source package, sales are final after successful private delivery. A refund may be offered for a duplicate payment, a package that cannot be delivered, a corrupt archive that cannot be replaced, or a material mismatch between the delivered package and the public description. Change-of-mind, unsupported environments, migration-provider decisions, and work outside the documented scope are not refundable. Network fees are not refundable. Crypto transfers are irreversible; always confirm the TRON (TRC20) network and destination before sending.

## Support boundary

Support covers installation and clarification of the documented v0.3.0 commands. It does not include custom detection rules, codebase remediation, payment-provider migration, transfer of customers or subscriptions, tax or legal advice, credential handling, data recovery, provider selection, guaranteed response times, or future versions. Bug reports may be submitted, but fixes and upgrades are not guaranteed as part of the purchase.

## Buyer responsibility

The buyer must scan only repositories and URLs they own or are authorized to inspect, keep the delivered package private, protect their own credentials, and verify the package checksum before use.
